title: CDS: An Anti-Aging Calibratable Digital Sensor for Detecting Multiple Types of Fault Injection Attacks
problem: Existing fault injection attack detectors suffer from aging-induced accuracy degradation, require complicated calibration procedures, and fail under dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) due to fixed delay chains that cannot adapt to voltage and frequency variations.
motivation: Fault injection attacks represent a critical threat to hardware security by enabling security feature circumvention, privilege escalation, and secret data extraction.
method: CDS works by measuring timing delays in a chain of logic gates within a chip, detecting when those delays change unexpectedly—a sign that an attacker is trying to inject faults via voltage spikes or laser glitches. As chips naturally age over time, their timing characteristics degrade, so CDS includes a calibration module that regularly resets its detection thresholds to stay accurate. It also includes a dynamic adjustment module that adapts in real time as the chip's power supply voltage and clock speed vary during normal operation, ensuring fault detection stays reliable even under these changing conditions. The sensor was tested in simulation protecting a PRESENT cryptographic algorithm accelerator against voltage and laser glitching attacks.
key_novelty: CDS keeps delay-chain fault sensors reliable by adding automatic compensation for chip aging and real-time adaptation to voltage and frequency variations.
contributions: Anti-aging delay-chain digital sensor (CDS) for detecting multiple fault injection attack types
Calibration module to mitigate aging-induced accuracy degradation
Dynamic adjustment mechanism for DVFS voltage and frequency adaptation
100% detection rate for voltage and laser glitching attacks with 1.1% false alarm increase after 7 years

metrics.accuracy: 100% detection for voltage and laser glitching; 1.1% false alarm rate increase after 7 years
metrics.other: 4.1% early warning for voltage glitching; 9.1% early warning for laser glitching

limitations: Evaluated through HSPICE simulation only; silicon implementation, area overhead, and power consumption analysis not discussed.
primary_theme: Anti-aging fault injection detection with DVFS adaptation
